title: Exporter hardening: audit-log-exporter retries/backpressure + per-sink delivery metrics + configurable sinks
creator: Nadia Rahman
description:
Context
Audit logs are an enterprise requirement and must be reliable under burst load and during downstream sink failures. Today the audit-log-exporter has best-effort delivery behavior and limited visibility. We need to harden it for: (1) retries/backoff, (2) backpressure so we don’t OOM or silently drop, (3) per-sink delivery metrics and structured errors, and (4) configurable sink destinations (S3, webhook, Splunk HEC) with consistent semantics.

Scope
- Exporter service only (export stage). Ingest/validate/store are tracked separately.
- Support multiple sinks per org with independent health + retry behavior.
- Provide clear semantics for delay vs drop (align with ENG-2489 SLO definitions).

Non-goals (this ticket)
- Customer UI for configuring sinks (Console work tracked elsewhere; we’ll expose config + APIs needed).
- Exactly-once delivery (we will provide at-least-once + idempotency guidance for sinks).

Requirements / Acceptance Criteria
1) Retry and backoff
- Implement exponential backoff with jitter per sink on retryable errors.
- Retryable vs non-retryable errors must be explicitly classified (HTTP 429/5xx retryable; auth/validation errors non-retryable).
- Configurable max retry window (default 24h) and per-attempt timeout.

2) Backpressure + durability
- No unbounded in-memory buffering.
- When downstream is unhealthy, exporter must apply backpressure to its own work queue and spill to a durable DLQ (dead-letter queue) for later replay.
- DLQ items must include sink_id, org_id, event_id, first_seen_at, last_attempt_at, attempt_count, last_error_class.
- Provide a safe replay mechanism (manual + automated) that respects rate limits.

3) Delivery metrics + structured errors
- Emit per-sink metrics:
  - audit_exporter_attempt_total{sink_type,sink_id,org_id,outcome}
  - audit_exporter_success_total{sink_type,sink_id,org_id}
  - audit_exporter_retry_total{sink_type,sink_id,org_id,error_class}
  - audit_exporter_dlq_enqueued_total{sink_type,sink_id,org_id,reason}
  - audit_exporter_latency_ms{sink_type,sink_id,org_id} (histogram)
  - audit_exporter_backlog_depth{sink_type,sink_id}
- Structured logs must include request_id where available, event_id, sink_id, org_id, error_class, and whether the event was retried vs DLQ’d.

4) Configurable sink destinations
- S3: multipart upload support where appropriate; robust handling for AccessDenied / bucket policy changes.
- Webhook: signed payload option (HMAC) and retry with 429 respect.
- Splunk HEC: token-based auth; batch send where safe; retry semantics.
- Configuration supports enabling/disabling sink without deploy.

5) Operational readiness
- Dashboards and alerts are set up (Grafana owned by SRE, but exporter must expose metrics).
- Runbook references exporter failure modes: backlog growth, DLQ growth, sink auth failures.
- Load test: demonstrate stable behavior at 5x expected peak export rate with a failing sink.

Implementation Notes
- Error classification will be centralized (shared package) so sink implementations use the same retry policy.
- Backpressure strategy:
  - Bounded worker concurrency per sink + global upper bound.
  - If backlog exceeds threshold, stop pulling new items for that sink and enqueue to DLQ for later drain.
- Batching:
  - Allow batching by sink if sink supports it (Splunk HEC), but preserve per-event IDs for traceability.

Rollout Plan
- Phase 0 (staging): enable new retry/backoff + metrics behind feature flag EXPORTER_RELIABILITY_V1.
- Phase 1 (prod, internal orgs): enable for Redwood internal orgs and 1 beta customer with S3 sink.
- Phase 2 (beta cohort): expand to remaining beta design partners; monitor DLQ and backlog dashboards daily.
- Phase 3 (GA): default-on for all enterprise orgs; keep ability to opt-out via config for 2 weeks.

comments: 2025-05-27 (Svetlana Petrenko): Proposed sink interface: ExportSink.Send(batch) -> (retryable bool, errorClass string, err error). Will keep per-event IDs in batch metadata for Splunk and webhook to preserve traceability.

2025-05-29 (Rafael Mendes): Please ensure we can distinguish exporter-induced delay vs upstream ingest delay. Add metric for time_in_export_queue_ms and tag with sink_id. This is needed for the delivery-lag SLO dashboard (ENG-2489).

2025-06-03 (Nadia Rahman): Confirmed with Security (Marcus) that DLQ payload must not contain secrets. DLQ entries may reference persisted event_id and sink metadata only; do not store full event payload twice unless encrypted at rest with the same controls as primary store.

2025-06-07 (Miles Thornton): Backpressure thresholds: start with per-sink backlog of 50k events or 15 minutes of sustained lag; at threshold, switch sink to 'degraded' and enqueue new work to DLQ while draining at controlled rate. Alert on sustained DLQ growth > 10 minutes.

2025-06-14 (Svetlana Petrenko): Implemented retry/backoff + DLQ in exporter branch. Added per-sink worker pools and bounded channels; confirmed no unbounded buffering in pprof. Next: add Splunk batching guardrails (max payload size) and explicit non-retryable classification for 4xx (except 429).

2025-06-21 (Aisha Bello): Dashboard wiring looks good; please add label cardinality limits. org_id can be high-cardinality; prefer org_tier and sink_id only for default dashboards. Keep org_id in logs, not metrics, or gate behind sampling in non-audit contexts (but audit metrics themselves should remain unsampled).

2025-06-24 (Svetlana Petrenko): Load test results in staging: webhook sink returning 500 for 30 minutes caused backlog growth but exporter remained stable; DLQ enqueued ~1.2M entries, replay drained in ~18 minutes after sink recovered. No drops observed; verified by event_id reconciliation against store.

2025-06-28 (Connor O'Brien): Approved for beta enablement with feature flag. Please coordinate with Rachel/Liam for first design partner enablement and confirm Splunk HEC token rotation does not create false 'non-retryable' spikes.

2025-07-02 (Svetlana Petrenko): Merged exporter PR (pr_232). Feature flag enabled for internal orgs + 1 beta customer. DLQ remained near zero after initial burst; retry counts aligned with expected 429 behavior on Splunk. Marking Done; follow-up: add replay UI endpoint and document idempotency expectations for webhook consumers (tracked in separate ticket).
